title: The names sulfites hide behind
standfirst: Sulfites goes by many names on a label. Here is the list we read for you.

spans.text: The law makes a maker name sulfites when they put it in on purpose. It does not make them use the word you are looking for.

blocks.label: names we watch for on a label
blocks.caption: Counted only where the link to sulfites is settled. Names that depend on the product are listed further down, and are not in this count.

resolved.method: Names whose link to sulfite is settled, counted from our allergen registry.
resolved.excludedNote: 9 more depend on the product or are shared with something else, so they are listed separately rather than counted here.

sources.doc: 21 CFR 101.100(a)(4) — Foods exempt from full ingredient labeling; sulfiting agents must be declared when present at ≥10 ppm total SO2
21 CFR 130.9 — Sulfites in standardized foods; declaration requirement

21 CFR 182.3616/182.3637/182.3739/182.3766/182.3798/182.3862 — GRAS sulfiting agents (potassium bisulfite, potassium metabisulfite, sodium bisulfite, sodium metabisulfite, sodium sulfite, sulfur dioxide)
Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 on food information to consumers, Annex II point 12 — Sulphur dioxide and sulphites at >10 mg/kg or 10 mg/L expressed as total SO2
Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008 on food additives, Annex II — E220 sulphur dioxide through E228 potassium hydrogen sulphite

Re-evaluation of sulfur dioxide (E 220), sodium sulfite (E 221), sodium bisulfite (E 222), sodium metabisulfite (E 223), potassium metabisulfite (E 224), calcium sulfite (E 226), calcium bisulfite (E 227) and potassium bisulfite (E 228) as food additives, EFSA Journal 14(4):4438
FALCPA (2004) and FASTER Act (2021) — establish the 9 major food allergens; sulfites are NOT among them and are regulated separately under 21 CFR 101.100
Sulfite sensitivity — hidden sources (dried fruit, wine, dehydrated potatoes, shrimp, bottled lemon/lime juice)

resolved.limit: We read what a label says. We cannot see what a maker left off it.

spans.text: These depend on the product. We treat them with care, and we say so on the label reading rather than guessing.
Names that look close but are not sulfites. These are the ones you can stop worrying about.
What we do when the label is unclear
If we cannot tell, we warn you. On this one thing we would rather be wrong in the direction of caution than quiet.
